messages:
Maya Chen: quick heads-up — ran a 30m perf profile on prod-us-west after the fused-attn kernel flip. noticing a shift: median batch size down ~18% and KV hit rate dropped from 0.91 -> 0.78 on the slice. p95 decode latency +120ms.

Kevin Patel: which model and which kernel variant did you flip to? any change to admission config?

Maya Chen: model: redwood-1b-open, kernel: fused-attn-v2 (hand-tuned CUDA kernels). no admission config change, same token_budget_target=512. ran the run against the same traffic replay for parity. attaching the small log snippet below and perf dash link.

Maya Chen: ```
batch_size_hist: {1: 42%, 2: 26%, 3-8: 24%, >8: 8%}
kv_cache_hit: 0.78
p50_decode_ms: 48
p95_decode_ms: 312
```

Maya Chen: perf dashboard: https://perf.internal/r/31235 (internal)

runtime-bot: canary flip to fused-attn-v2 completed 2026-03-17T09:04:12Z — 4 workers in canary pool.

Sasha Iqbal: hmm — fused kernel looks faster single-threaded but could be increasing decode rate variance. that could shrink batch formation window and cause smaller batches + more divergent KV access patterns, explaining the hit rate drop.

Tomasz Kowalski: can we capture a microprofile around admission + batching? something like: `./tools/profiler --span admission,batcher,kv --out s37.json --short` on a canary instance. need to see time spent in enqueue vs decode and the queue draining pattern.

Nora Li: from the classifier side, the prompt-length buckets are still using boundaries [0-64,65-256,257-1024]. with the increased decode-rate variance we should consider narrower short-bucket cut (0-32,33-96,97-256) so short requests coalesce better. also thinking of moving token_budget_target up for short buckets.

Kevin Patel: what's the quickest rollback if this degrades SLA more? can we fallback to fused-attn-v1 by config toggle?

Maya Chen: yes — rollout is via canary-flag. rollback is a single toggle and a restart of the canary pool (no infra change). PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/btn/5243

Sasha Iqbal: provisional experiment: keep kernel v2 in canary but change: token_budget_target_short=768, short_bucket_upper=32, admission_timeout_ms=12. If batch sizes recover, we keep kernel and tune. If not, rollback. estimate p95 down ~80ms if KV hit recovers >0.88.

Maya Chen: sounds good. I'll run a 1h test with that config on canary. command: `kubectl apply -f canary-config.yaml && tools/traffic-replay --slice prod-us-west --duration 1h`

Maya Chen: canary config snippet: ```yaml
admission: 
  token_budget_targets:
    short: 768
    mid: 512
    long: 256
buckets: 
  short_upper: 32
  mid_upper: 256
  long_upper: 1024
```

runtime-bot: experiment scheduled: exper-20260317-01 by maya. live window: 60m. notify: eng-runtime, eng-ml.

Tomasz Kowalski: I'll grab microprofiles when it runs. will also dump KV access heatmap to check priming/clustering.

Nora Li: I'll recalibrate the classifier thresholds offline against the replayed traffic and push a small model update if needed.

Kevin Patel: sgtm. if p95 stays worse after 1h, plan to rollback and open a postmortem. please @me on the experiment thread. :thumbsup:

Maya Chen: ack — starting now, will post quick results + KV hit graphs in this thread when done. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
